Thank you. Thank you, Chair Davey, and thank you, Members of Council, for the opportunity to speak today.
As you're aware, Canada Post has increased their posted charges by 25% starting January 1, 2025.
The city spent approximately $1 million in postage in 2024.
The majority of the postage budget relates to the mailing of tax and utility bills.
It costs approximately $1.50 to mail out a paper bill.
At this time, approximately 50% of our residents are enrolled on e-billing.
The report in front of you today exposed the feasibility of charging a fee for paper bills.
So what does legislation say?
So the Municipal Act provides direction on how property tax bills are to be delivered.
Section 343.1 of the Act requires the Treasurer to send a tax bill to every taxpayer.
Section 343.6.1 allows the Treasurer to send a tax bill to the taxpayer electronically
if the taxpayer has chosen to receive the tax bill in that manner.
So what this implies is that the permission must be given from the taxpayer to enroll on e-billing.
Section 343.7 requires that where a taxpayer directs the treasurer in writing to send a taxpayer's tax bill by registered mail,
we can add the cost of the registered mail to the property tax account.
So because 343.7 directly references mailing costs and when to charge them, and as there's no mention of fees related to mailing of standard bills,
City staff's position is that such fees are not authorized on standard bills, although there is no explicit prohibition in the Act to charge fees for standard bills.
The Ontario Energy Board, or the OAB, provides direction to gas utilities on how the utility
bills are to be delivered.
The OAB has previously ruled that Enbridge could not charge customers for paper bills,
nor can they automatically enroll customers on e-billing.
Again, the implication here is that permission must be granted by the rate payer to enroll
them on e-billing.
Kitchener Utilities follows and adheres to OEB decisions.
Unlike Kitchener, most municipalities owned, most municipally owned utilities across the
province do not provide gas and therefore are not obligated to follow OEB decisions.
So this slide, this slide shows e-billing enrollment for the municipalities.
As you can see, Kitchener has the highest enrollment on e-billing at almost 50% in this
comparative group. None of the municipalities in this group charge fee for paper bills.
This table shows municipalities who do charge or are going to charge a fee for a paper bill.
The city of Quint West charges $1.50 for utility bills only. Sioux Lookout charges $3 for property
tax and utility bills. And the township of Wilmot has not yet started charging a fee
for paper bills but has approved this fee through the 2025 budget process.
Again, these municipalities only have water utility
and therefore not subject to OAB rulings with respect to utility bills.
So staff investigated the feasibility of three options.
Option one, which was to charge $2 for every paper bill to be mailed out.
And option two, grandfathering existing customers
and charging new customers a fee. Both these options are not inconsistent with legislation
and the OEB's previous ruling. The recommended option is option three, which is to enhance the
promotion of e-billing to a targeted marketing campaign. So this option offers a balanced
approach, avoids creating any new financial barriers, is most inclusive, financially
responsible and helps protect the environment. It also aligns with the OEB's
past decision and does not appear to conflict with any legislation.
So to implement option three staff will develop a multi-channel
communication strategy which includes for example, I'm almost done, offering
incentives such as contests, inserts in utility and property tax bills, in-person
and telephone support for residents.
Although we have one of the highest e-billing enrollment rates in the province, we believe
we can still do better.
Therefore we strongly, we feel strongly that this communication strategy is and will help
continue to increase e-billing enrollment.
And that concludes my presentation.
